outcome: No accepted resolution exists. Since 26 Jan 2024 three unrefereed claims of an unconditional proof of infinitude have appeared (Wayne Lewis's arXiv paper 'Global Primitive Roots of Unity', first carrying the claim in v20 of 23 Jul 2025, together with his seminar talk of 19 Dec 2025; a 2025 mathlog blog post that rests on Cramér's conjecture; and a 2011 arXiv paper by Shan-Guang Tan whose Sophie Germain corollary I could not verify), and none has been publicly engaged with; the conditional and neighbouring results found are listed below, and Wikipedia's article still says the infinitude 'has not been proven'.
problem_asks: Two questions in one bullet, which are equivalent. (1) Are there infinitely many Sophie Germain primes, i.e. primes p such that 2p+1 is also prime? (2) Are there infinitely many safe primes, i.e. primes q of the form 2p+1 with p prime, equivalently primes q such that (q-1)/2 is also prime? The map p to 2p+1 is a bijection between the two sets (apart from the small exceptions), so a proof of either settles both. The bullet asks only for infinitude: no counting asymptotic is requested, and the heuristic density of about 2C x/(log x)^2 with C about 0.66 (Bateman-Horn) is not part of the question.

events.what_happened: Wayne Lewis (Honolulu Community College, University of Hawai'i), 'Global Primitive Roots of Unity', arXiv:2411.16000, first posted 24 Nov 2024 with no Sophie Germain claim. The claim is introduced in version 20 (revised 23 Jul 2025): the abstract lists 'positive resolutions of the infinitude of (i) Sophie Germain primes = 1 (mod 4), (ii) Sophie Germain primes = 3 (mod 4), (iii) composite Mersenne numbers 2^p-1, (iv) pairs (p-2,p)'. The v20 body (Section 6) defines a Sophie Germain prime as q = (p-1)/2 with p prime, states Proposition 6.3 'There are infinitely many Sophie Germain primes congruent to' 1 and 3 mod 4, and ends the 3 mod 4 case with 'so there are infinitely many Sophie Germain primes'. Remark 6.1 of v20 is conditional on a quantity nu being prime. Version 25 (28 Aug 2025) and 30 (9 Oct 2025) abstracts list 'positive resolutions of the conjectured infinitude of primes p for which (p-1)/2 is prime' together with a primitive-root result, and drop the twin-prime and Mersenne items. Version 38 (19 Jan 2026) abstract lists '(p-1)/6 is prime' and not (p-1)/2, but its body keeps the Sophie Germain claim as Corollary 6.4 (a Sophie Germain prime is q = (p-1)/2 with p prime), whose proof ends 'It then follows via Łoś's theorem that there are infinitely many Sophie Germain primes'; Theorem 6.3 concerns (p-1)/6 and is described as a separate result. The arXiv abstract page for v44 (revised 14 Aug 2026) was opened; its body was not re-read.
events.revisions: v1 24 Nov 2024 (no SG claim); v2 26 Nov 2024 (no SG); v10 16 Apr 2025 (no SG in abstract); v15 29 May 2025, v17 28 Jun 2025, v18 6 Jul 2025, v19 13 Jul 2025 (no SG in abstracts; v15-v19 bodies not read); v20 23 Jul 2025 (SG claims first appear in abstract and Section 6); v25 28 Aug 2025 (abstract: (p-1)/2); v30 9 Oct 2025 (same); v38 19 Jan 2026 (abstract: (p-1)/6; body Corollary 6.4: (p-1)/2); v44 14 Aug 2026 (abstract page only). The date recorded is the v20 revision date; the claim is absent from the abstracts of every earlier version I opened, so the first version carrying the body argument may be v20 or a later version between v19 and v20.
events.delivers: Claims the unrestricted infinitude of Sophie Germain primes (equivalently of safe primes). In v20 this is argued by two residue classes, 1 mod 4 and 3 mod 4, which together cover all odd Sophie Germain primes, so as written it is the full statement and not a restricted case. In v38 it is Corollary 6.4, which the proof says follows from Proposition 4.4 and Theorem 6.3 and 'can be adjusted by taking only the quadratic families S_p for 3 != p in P', and is described as an adjustment 'rather than fully rechecked'. The method is a nonprincipal ultrafilter on the primes (Theorem 5.3), an ultraproduct valued field, and Los's theorem; I did not check Section 5 or the adjustment.
events.remains: If the Corollary 6.4 argument holds, nothing remains of either part, since the two parts are equivalent. If it fails, both parts remain open. The v38 abstract's (p-1)/6 result is a different statement and does not settle the Sophie Germain question. The abstract and the body disagree on which of (p-1)/2 and (p-1)/6 is proved, and the record cannot say which the author stands behind.
events.time_since_posted: about 14 months since the v20 revision (23 Jul 2025 to 10 Oct 2026); no public engagement found in searches of arXiv listings, the Erdos problem forum, or the search engine. The Erdos forum comment of 1 Nov 2025 treats infinitude as expected under Bateman-Horn, which is a heuristic and not engagement with this argument.
events.doubts: (1) The abstract and body disagree: the v38 abstract lists only (p-1)/6, while the body claims (p-1)/2 by Corollary 6.4. (2) Scope changed between versions: the v20 abstract announced positive resolutions for twin pairs (p-2,p) and composite Mersenne numbers 2^p-1, both famous open problems; these items are absent from the abstracts of v25 onward. (3) The body describes the Corollary 6.4 argument as 'an adjustment rather than fully rechecked' (verbatim in the v38 proof text). (4) The claimed infinitude depends on the ultrafilter in Section 5, which I did not check. (5) No Lean or other formal check was found. These are signals for the judging pass; I have not weighed them.
events.direction: Asserts the infinitude the problem asks about, so it cuts in the direction the conjecture predicts. It is a claimed resolution of the whole bullet if it stands.

events.what_happened: A Japanese-language post on mathlog.info titled 'Definitive proof about Sophie Germain primes', in the site's unsolved-problem explainer category, by an author I could not identify, claiming that Sophie Germain primes and safe primes are both infinite. Per search-tool excerpts (the page did not load in three fetch attempts, so I did not read it): it first shows that for n of at least 9 there are at least three odd integers of the form 2p+1 between 2p_n and 3p_n, then invokes Cramér's conjecture in the bound p_(n+1) - p_n < (log p_n)^2 - log p_n to conclude that one of several consecutive candidates must be safe. The excerpt also says the site hosts unreviewed 'Proof of Cramér's conjecture' posts.
events.delivers: If the excerpt is accurate, a conditional argument: the infinitude follows from Cramér's conjecture (open), not unconditionally.
events.remains: Unconditional infinitude of both parts. Conditionally on Cramér's conjecture, the infinitude would follow, if the argument holds.

events.doubts: The argument rests on Cramér's conjecture, which is unproven, as the excerpt itself indicates. The excerpt is cut off, so I could not check the final inequality chain. The title overstates a conditional argument. The site is an unreviewed blog. The month of 2025 comes from a search summary and is unverified.

events.what_happened: Shan-Guang Tan (Zhejiang University), arXiv:1110.3465, first posted 16 Oct 2011 as 'A proof of the Goldbach conjecture' (9 pages). Later versions carry the title 'On the solution of the Collatz problem' (v20 onward; latest v32 revised 29 Dec 2025), which claims the Collatz problem is solved. A search-tool excerpt of the latest PDF reports a closing-section corollary: since a prime-counting function for a polynomial family tends to infinity, infinitely many m make 2m+1 and 4m+3 prime, so p = 2m+1 gives infinitely many Sophie Germain primes of the form 2p+1 with p prime. The corollary depends on a main theorem about prime values of polynomials, which the excerpt names only as part of the Tan series. I could not read the corollary: the PDF is not decodable by my tools, and the HTML renderings (v26, v32) end at Lemma 3.25 and contain no Sophie Germain passage. The abstracts of v1, v23 (12 Jun 2024) and v25 (23 Jan 2025) do not mention Sophie Germain primes.

events.what_happened: Aradhya Goel (IIT Kanpur), 'Sophie Germain Primes and the Totient of Fibonacci Numbers', arXiv:2604.17847, v1 20 Apr 2026, v2 21 Apr 2026, v3 22 Apr 2026. For a Sophie Germain prime q: if z(2q+1) divides pi(q), then the set S(q) is a nonempty arithmetic progression, with odd cardinality and q = 8 mod 15 for q > 5, and a converse. The conjecture that S(q) nonempty forces a prime p = 1 mod q with z(p) dividing pi(q) is checked for q up to 50000. Conditionally on the Sophie Germain conjecture, infinitely many primes q = 8 mod 15 with a Fibonacci divisibility condition follow.
events.delivers: Does not establish infinitude. It proves structural statements about the Sophie Germain primes q that satisfy a divisibility condition, and it derives conditional consequences from the Sophie Germain conjecture. The condition is verified computationally for about 23.9% of the Sophie Germain primes tested.
events.doubts: Conditional statements and computation only, as the abstract says; the abstract page was read, the body was not.
events.direction: Neither settles nor cuts against the bullet. It reduces a different statement to the Sophie Germain conjecture.

events.what_happened: Josue Alexander Ibarra, 'A counterexample to a subadditivity conjecture of Cohen for Sophie Germain cyclic numbers', arXiv:2607.09793, 9 Jul 2026. A Sophie Germain cyclic number is one where both n and 2n+1 are cyclic. The paper refutes Cohen's subadditivity conjecture for the counting function of these numbers, with counterexample m = 31, n = 3928, and states that the argument is verified by the Lean 4 kernel with an ancillary file anc/cohen66.lean.
events.revisions: v1 only as far as read.
events.delivers: A counterexample for a counting function on Sophie Germain cyclic numbers, which are a different object from Sophie Germain primes. It says nothing about the infinitude of Sophie Germain primes.

machine_checked.note: the abstract says the argument is verified by the Lean 4 kernel; I did not open the ancillary file, so sorry-freeness is not checked

events.directly_checkable: Counterexample m = 31, n = 3928 for the subadditivity inequality on the counting function of Sophie Germain cyclic numbers; checkable by hand in principle.
events.direction: Neighbouring object; does not cut for or against infinitude of Sophie Germain primes.
events.object: A pair m = 31, n = 3928 whose Sophie Germain cyclic number count up to 3959 exceeds the sum of the counts up to 31 and up to 3928, refuting Cohen's conjecture for that counting function. It is explicit.

events.what_happened: Paolo Leonetti, 'A characterization of Sophie Germain primes - II', arXiv v1 25 Jul 2026. For even n at least 4, the list 1^sigma(1), ..., n^sigma(n) is a complete residue system mod n for some permutation sigma if and only if n/2 is prime and n/2 - 1 is squarefree. It complements a 2018 result for odd n.
events.revisions: v1 only as far as read.
events.delivers: A residue-system characterisation of even n. It uses the prime n/2 but contains no statement about the infinitude of Sophie Germain primes.
events.direction: Neighbouring statement only; neither cuts for nor against infinitude.

events.what_happened: A background almost-prime result, as cited in A. J. Irving, 'Almost-prime values of polynomials at prime arguments', arXiv:1410.3333 (13 Oct 2014), introduction: 'it was shown by Richert [7, Theorem 7] that f(p) is infinitely often a P_{2 deg f+1}'. For a linear f = 2p+1 this gives infinitely many primes p with 2p+1 having at most three prime factors. disputes.summary: Three unrefereed claims of the same unconditional infinitude exist and do not agree with each other or with the bodies of the papers that make them: Lewis's arXiv paper (v20 onward; the abstract changes between (p-1)/2 and (p-1)/6 while the body keeps (p-1)/2); Lewis's 19 Dec 2025 talk, which cites no preprint; and the Tan arXiv paper (corollary reported in a search excerpt, not verified). The 2025 mathlog post makes a conditional claim on Cramér's conjecture. No priority dispute is recorded because each claimant's work postdates the open-problem status in the cited sources.

summary: Nothing has been settled in the literature that I could find. The Wikipedia article 'Safe and Sophie Germain primes' (opened; undated, so its revision date is not known) says the infinitude 'has not been proven', and no source found after 26 Jan 2024 calls it solved. The only candidate resolutions are unrefereed. (1) Wayne Lewis, 'Global Primitive Roots of Unity' (arXiv:2411.16000). The first posting (24 Nov 2024) makes no Sophie Germain claim. The claim appears with v20 (revised 23 Jul 2025), with Proposition 6.3 covering residue classes 1 and 3 mod 4 (together all odd Sophie Germain primes). Later versions keep it: v25 and v30 abstracts list (p-1)/2, and v38 (19 Jan 2026) has Corollary 6.4 claiming (p-1)/2 via Los's theorem while its abstract lists only (p-1)/6. The v20 abstract also announced positive resolutions for twin pairs and composite Mersenne numbers, which are absent from v25 onward. Lewis's seminar talk of 19 Dec 2025 describes an ultraproduct proof and cites no preprint. Nobody publicly engaged with it in about 14 months. (2) A 2025 mathlog blog post titled 'Definitive proof about Sophie Germain primes' whose argument, per search excerpts, rests on Cramér's conjecture. I could not open the page, so its month of 2025 and its text are unverified. (3) Shan-Guang Tan, arXiv:1110.3465, first posted 16 Oct 2011 as a Goldbach proof and later a Collatz proof. A search excerpt says its latest version has a Sophie Germain corollary. I could not read that passage in any version, and no abstract I could read mentions it, so this is the weakest of the three. Close call: Lewis's argument is an ultrafilter-and-Los argument of a kind the author has used before; against it stand the abstract-body mismatch on (p-1)/2 versus (p-1)/6, the body's own words that the key adjustment is 'presented as an adjustment rather than fully rechecked', and the lack of any public check. Conditional and neighbouring work: Goel (Apr 2026, conditional on the Sophie Germain conjecture); Carella (2023, finite lower bound up to x); Bordignon and Lee (2022, upper bound up to x); Agoh (Integers, 2025, on the complement set, not read); Ibarra (Jul 2026, cyclic-number analogue, Lean-verified); Leonetti (Jul 2026) and Clerc (Mar 2026), structural results; Grantham and Graves (2019, Brazilian Sophie Germain primes); Varney (2016 thesis, conditional on Siegel zeros, not opened); and an older Richert result, cited by Irving (2014), giving infinitely many primes p with 2p+1 having at most three prime factors. AI: the only AI-credited Sophie Germain paper I found is the Fujimoto dev.to draft (17 Jun 2026) with 'Claude Opus (Anthropic)' and 'chat-Claude (Anthropic, articulation thread 2026-06-17)' as co-authors. It reports empirical observations and disclaims any progress on infinitude, so it bears on this bullet only as a disclaimed non-result. No source credits an AI system with any infinitude claim. Lewis's paper, talk, and Tan's paper name no AI system in the text I could read. Erdos forum thread 1065 (1 Nov 2025) only repeats the Bateman-Horn expectation. Maynard gave a public lecture on 1 Apr 2026 billed as covering 'progress towards resolving the questions' Germain asked, but I found no content and could not reach the recording. Observation outside the bullet for the judging pass: the search engine also surfaced an Oct 2025 optimization preprint and an AxiomProver prime-gap item (Aug 2026), but neither is about Sophie Germain primes; the optimization preprint's abstract does not mention safe primes, contrary to one search summary.
competing_reading: Read as resolved: Lewis's Corollary 6.4 is a complete ultrafilter argument for the unrestricted infinitude, and the v38 abstract's (p-1)/6 result is just a different emphasis within the same framework. The talk, the mathlog post and the Tan corollary would then be independent restatements or noise. Lack of engagement after 14 months is normal for a niche arXiv paper in number theory. Read as not resolved: the abstract and the body disagree on which statement is proved; the one place the body names an unverified step is the Section 5 adjustment; the twin-prime and Mersenne claims in the v20 abstract were dropped without explanation; no expert, journal, or formal check exists; and the other two claimants are weaker still. On the evidence I have, the second reading is the one the record supports.
what_would_settle_it: (a) A public verification of Corollary 6.4 in arXiv:2411.16000 (v38 or later), in particular the Section 5 ultrafilter theorem and the 'adjusted' finite-intersection argument, from an expert or a journal referee. (b) An explanation of why the v38 abstract lists (p-1)/6 while the body proves (p-1)/2, and of the dropped twin-prime and Mersenne claims. (c) The Lewis talk recording or slides from 19 Dec 2025. (d) The first version of arXiv:1110.3465 that carries a Sophie Germain corollary, and the text of that corollary and its main theorem.
